standard.name: Independent Bernoulli randomization at probability one half

assumptions.condition: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).

standard.name: Li--Wager independent unit-type and response sampling with uniform latent types

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

standard.name: Li--Wager bounded response and derivative envelope through order two
Known \(C^3\) radius separated from the lower-order response envelope

definitions.name: Li--Wager known-rank \(C^3\) class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).  This is the bounded, row-regular, known-rank, two-radius subclass of the Li--Wager sampling family selected by those properties; it is not a claim that the displayed class equals the full class used in LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Li--Wager finite indirect-effect benchmark
definitions.construction: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Exact realized-degree support correction
definitions.construction: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact symmetric discrete local-polynomial score
definitions.construction: For \(N_i>0\), let \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}\mid A]\) and \(q_{i,h}=V_i\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}/\mu_{2,i}(h)\). For \(N_i=0\), set \(q_{i,h}=0\) and \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=0\).

definitions.name: Deterministically selected observed principal-component projector
definitions.construction:
Put \(m_{r,n}=\min\{r,n\}\).  Order the \(n\) eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_{r,n}}\) contain the first \(m_{r,n}\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
Thus \(\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto the leading \(\min\{r,n\}\)-dimensional eigenspace selected by this convention.  The deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map for every \(r,n\in\mathbb N\), without requiring \(r\leq n\).

definitions.name: Explicit first-projection PC handle with bounded-difference certificate
Feasible explicit first-projection PC estimator
definitions.construction:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]

definitions.name: Graph-observable degree-exact radii for the explicit PC handle
definitions.construction:
For the explicit certificates in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), set
\[
 \overline b_h(A)=\frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
\]
and
\[
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\]
Thus \(\overline s_h(A)\) is a finite-sample conditional standard-deviation certificate, not an asserted sharp-rate formula.

definitions.name: Oracle degree-exact optimal base bandwidth
definitions.construction:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), define
\[
 h^\dagger=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)].
\]
This is the oracle full-class radius-minimizing bandwidth.  Its evaluation requires the full-class supremum and is not an operational data-driven tuning rule.

definitions.name: Supported and oracle degree-exact full-class envelopes
Nonempty-class absolute-risk and honest expected interval-length criteria
definitions.construction: At every index for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), let \(D=(A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\). Define \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\), where the infimum ranges over all real-valued measurable estimators \(\widetilde\theta=\widetilde\theta(D)\). Define \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[u(D)-\ell(D)]\), where the infimum ranges over data-measurable closed intervals \(\mathcal C(D)=[\ell(D),u(D)]\) with finite measurable endpoints \(\ell(D)\leq u(D)\) and satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C(D)\}\geq1-\alpha\). For every such interval, \(\operatorname{length}\{\mathcal C(D)\}=u(D)-\ell(D)\).

statements.statement: For every \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i\ge1\) and every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), the exact support correction gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\). Symmetry of \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N_i,1/2)\) yields \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\), and \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]=\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\). For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)|\le Lh_i(h)^2/6\).
statements.justification: This establishes exact derivative moments at every positive realized degree and removes the zero-normalizer failure at the lower bandwidth endpoint.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph uses an unlocalized global binomial score; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest does not face a random degree lattice.
statements.consumer: It supplies the unitwise bias and exact inverse-moment contribution in the feasible-PC certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i=N\geq1\), fix \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), and condition on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions.  By \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\),
\[
 M_i\mid A\sim {\rm Binomial}(N,1/2),\qquad V_i=M_i/N-1/2.
\]
If \(N\) is even, the nearest nonzero exposure-lattice points are \(\pm N^{-1}\); if \(N\) is odd, they are \(\pm(2N)^{-1}\).  Each has strictly positive binomial probability.  Hence \({\rm def:lattice\text{-}radius}\) implies
\[
 \Pr_Z\{0<|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\mid A\}>0,
\]
and the nonnegative summands in \({\rm def:discrete\text{-}score}\) give \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\).

The involution \(M_i\mapsto N-M_i\) preserves binomial probability and sends \(V_i\) to \(-V_i\).  The truncation indicator is even and \(q_{i,h}\) is odd.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=1,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^3\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)^2}
 =\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}.
\]
Every division is valid by the strict positivity just proved.

Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Taylor's formula with integral remainder, together with \({\rm ass:third\text{-}derivative\text{-}bound}\), gives for \(v\in[-1/2,1/2]\)
\[
 f_i(a,1/2+v)=f_i(a,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)v
 +\frac12\partial_x^2f_i(a,1/2)v^2+R_i(a,v),
 \qquad |R_i(a,v)|\leq \frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplication by \(q_{i,h}\), conditional expectation, and the three preceding moment identities show
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A].
\]
On the support of \(q_{i,h}\), \(|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\).  Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A]\right|
 &\leq \frac{L}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[|V_i|^4\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]\\
 &\leq \frac{Lh_i(h)^2}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]
 =\frac L6h_i(h)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves all claimed moment and bias identities.

statements.statement:
Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy
\[
 \left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|
 \le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac{1}{N_i}
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}.
\]
Moreover, along any maintained triangular-array sequence with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) such that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1/2\), one has \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\). On the further intersection of such a sequence with every source hypothesis enumerated in \({\rm lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\), specialized to treatment probability one half and with the published normalization well defined, the additive form of Slutsky's argument transfers Li--Wager's equation~(43) Gaussian limits from centering at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) to centering at \(\theta_n\). This is an asymptotic comparator only on that intersection, not a theorem for every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), and it is not a finite-sample equality of the two targets.
statements.justification: The bridge separates a maintained-class center approximation from use of the published Gaussian theorem, so the latter is invoked only where every source condition holds.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Proposition~1 gives a minimum-degree approximation; the displayed degree-exact symmetric remainder keeps isolates visible and does not identify the two finite-sample targets. Its Theorem~6 applies only under the full source conditions recorded in the cited lemma.
statements.consumer: It permits asymptotic comparison with Li--Wager equation~(43) only on the stated class intersection while keeping the finite-population derivative as a distinct target everywhere.
statements.proof_tex:
Work first conditionally on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), and define the proof-intermediate function
\[
 g_i(x):=\frac{f_i(1,x)+f_i(0,x)}{2},\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\), conditional on \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) and \(A\), every assignment vector has probability \(2^{-n}\). This probability does not depend on the latent types. The conditional-expectation identity
\[
 \Pr\!\left(Z=z\mid A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right)
 =\mathbb E\!\left[
 \Pr\!\left(Z=z\mid A,(U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right)
 \mathrel{\big|}A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \right]
 =2^{-n}
\]
therefore shows that the assignment remains product Bernoulli conditional on \(A\) and the response functions.

Fix \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i=m>0\). Because \(A_{ii}=0\), \(M_i\) is a function only of \((Z_j)_{j\ne i}\). Hence \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\) gives
\[
 M_i\sim {\rm Binomial}(m,1/2)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 Z_i\ \text{is independent of}\ M_i
\]
under the conditional law just obtained. Define the unit-level contribution
\[
 \beta_i:=4\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
 Y_i(Z)(M_i-m/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \right].
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:anonymous-interference}\), \(Y_i(Z)=f_i(Z_i,1/2+V_i)\) for this nonisolated unit. Averaging first over the independent variable \(Z_i\) replaces this outcome by \(g_i(1/2+V_i)\), while the definition of \(V_i\) gives \(M_i-m/2=mV_i\). Consequently,
\[
 \beta_i
 =4m\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[
 g_i(1/2+V_i)V_i\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \right].
\]
If \(N_i=0\), then \(M_i-N_i/2=0\), so set \(\beta_i=0\). The construction in \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\) now yields
\[
 \bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_i.
\]

For the fixed nonisolated unit, let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be independent random variables taking the values \(-1/2\) and \(1/2\) with equal probability, and put \(S_m=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j\). The preceding binomial law shows that \(V_i\) has the law of \(S_m/m\). Centering and independence give
\[
 \mathbb E S_m^2=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^2=\frac m4,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E S_m^3=0.
\]
In the fourth-power expansion, the only terms with nonzero expectation are the one-index terms and the terms consisting of two pairs. Since \(\mathbb E X_j^2=1/4\) and \(\mathbb E X_j^4=1/16\),
\[
 \mathbb E S_m^4
 =\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
 +6\sum_{1\le j<k\le m}\mathbb E X_j^2\mathbb E X_k^2
 =\frac{3m^2-2m}{16}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathbb E V_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E V_i^2=\frac1{4m},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E V_i^3=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E V_i^4=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16m^4}\le\frac3{16m^2}.
\]

By \(\texttt{ass:third-derivative-bound}\) and the definition of \(g_i\),
\[
 \sup_{x\in[0,1]}\left|g_i^{(3)}(x)\right|\le L.
\]
Repeated integration of the third derivative on the segment joining \(1/2\) and \(1/2+v\), which is contained in \([0,1]\) for \(v\in[-1/2,1/2]\), gives
\[
 g_i(1/2+v)
 =g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+\frac12g_i''(1/2)v^2+R_i(v),
 \qquad
 |R_i(v)|\le\frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplying by \(v\), taking the conditional expectation, and using the four moment identities above makes the constant and quadratic Taylor terms vanish and gives \(4m\mathbb E V_i^2=1\). Therefore
\[
 \beta_i-g_i'(1/2)
 =4m\,\mathbb E\!\left[V_iR_i(V_i)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right],
\]
and hence
\[
 \left|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)\right|
 \le \frac{4mL}{6}\mathbb E V_i^4
 \le \frac{4mL}{6}\frac3{16m^2}
 =\frac{L}{8m}.
\]
By \(\texttt{def:target}\), the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\theta_n\) is \(g_i'(1/2)\). For an isolated unit, \(\texttt{ass:response-envelope}\) gives
\[
 |g_i'(1/2)|
 \le\frac{|\partial_xf_i(1,1/2)|+|\partial_xf_i(0,1/2)|}{2}
 \le B.
\]
Separating the nonisolated and isolated vertices and applying the triangle inequality proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|
 &\le \frac1n\sum_{i:N_i>0}\left|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)\right|
 +\frac1n\sum_{i:N_i=0}|g_i'(1/2)|\\
 &\le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
 +\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

We next derive an auxiliary bound involving only the fixed lower-order envelope. By \(\texttt{ass:response-envelope}\), \(\sup_x|g_i''(x)|\le B\). Integrating the second derivative gives
\[
 g_i(1/2+v)=g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+T_i(v),
 \qquad
 |T_i(v)|\le\frac B2v^2.
\]
The same moment cancellation as above, followed by \(\mathbb E|V_i|^3\le(\mathbb EV_i^4)^{3/4}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
 &\le 2mB\,\mathbb E|V_i|^3
 \le 2mB\,(\mathbb E V_i^4)^{3/4}\\
 &\le 2mB\left(\frac3{16m^2}\right)^{3/4}
 =\frac{3^{3/4}B}{4\sqrt m}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Consider now any maintained triangular-array sequence with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) and with
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log\rho_n}{\log n}>-\frac12.
\]
Choose \(\varepsilon>0\) smaller than the gap between this lower limit and \(-1/2\). Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_n\ge n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
Fix a vertex \(i\). By the independent uniform latent types in \(\texttt{ass:unit-sampling}\) and conditional edge independence in \(\texttt{ass:graphon-draw}\), after conditioning only on \(U_i=u\), the pairs consisting of \(U_j\) and the edge draw \(A_{ij}\), for \(j\ne i\), are independent and identically distributed. Marginalizing each \(U_j\) therefore gives
\[
 N_i\mid U_i=u\sim {\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n(u)),
 \qquad
 p_n(u):=\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv.
\]
The conditions \(\texttt{ass:kernel-bound}\) and \(\texttt{ass:edge-probability}\) imply \(0\le p_n(u)\le\rho_n\kappa\le1\). Moreover, \(\texttt{ass:degree-regularity}\) gives, for almost every \(u\),
\[
 \mu_i(u):=\mathbb E[N_i\mid U_i=u]
 =(n-1)p_n(u)
 \ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{\kappa}.
\]
Because every \(U_i\) is uniform by \(\texttt{ass:unit-sampling}\), this almost-everywhere inequality applies to all finitely many realized types with probability one at each \(n\).

For completeness, derive the required binomial lower-tail estimate. If \(S\sim{\rm Binomial}(m,p)\), \(\mu=mp\), and \(t=\log2\), then pointwise
\[
 \mathbf1\{S\le\mu/2\}\le \exp\{t(\mu/2-S)\}.
\]
Taking expectations, using independence of the Bernoulli summands, and applying \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr(S\le\mu/2)
 &\le e^{t\mu/2}\mathbb E e^{-tS}
 =e^{t\mu/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^m\\
 &\le\exp\!\left\{\frac{t\mu}{2}-\mu(1-e^{-t})\right\}
 =\exp\!\left\{-\frac{1-\log2}{2}\mu\right\}
 \le e^{-\mu/8},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last step uses \((1-\log2)/2\ge1/8\). Since \(\mu_i(u)\ge(n-1)\rho_n/\kappa\), the event
\[
 \left\{N_i<\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{2\kappa}\right\}
\]
is contained in \(\{N_i<\mu_i(u)/2\}\). Applying the preceding estimate conditionally on \(U_i\), integrating over \(U_i\), and taking a union bound yield, for
\[
 \mathcal E_n:=\left\{\min_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i
 \ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{2\kappa}\right\},
\]
the probability bound
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal E_n^c)
 \le n\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{8\kappa}\right\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Indeed, the exponent diverges at least as a fixed multiple of \(n^{1/2+\varepsilon}\), which dominates \(\log n\).

On \(\mathcal E_n\) there are no isolated vertices and
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\frac1{\sqrt{N_i}}
 \le\left(\frac{2\kappa}{(n-1)\rho_n}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The auxiliary response-envelope bound thus implies
\[
 \frac{\left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|}{\sqrt{\rho_n}}
 \le\frac{3^{3/4}B\sqrt{2\kappa}}{4\sqrt{n-1}\,\rho_n}
 \le\frac{3^{3/4}B\sqrt{2\kappa}}{4\sqrt{1-1/n}\,n^{\varepsilon}}
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{on }\mathcal E_n.
\]
Together with \(\Pr(\mathcal E_n^c)\to0\), this proves, independently of the additional Li--Wager source conditions,
\[
 \bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n}).
\]

Finally restrict to the further intersection with every source condition recorded in \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\), specialize the source treatment probability to one half as required by \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\), and suppose the equation~(43) normalization is well defined. The cited lemma then supplies the published standardized Gaussian limit centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\), with the change of center measured on the \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale. The last display says that replacing that center by \(\theta_n\) adds a term converging to zero in probability in the same normalization. To verify the additive limit step directly, write the published standardized statistic as \(T_n\), the normalized center change as \(R_n=o_P(1)\), and let \(\Phi\) be the standard-normal distribution function. For every real \(x\) and every \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \Pr(T_n\le x-\eta)-\Pr(|R_n|>\eta)
 \le \Pr(T_n+R_n\le x)
 \le \Pr(T_n\le x+\eta)+\Pr(|R_n|>\eta).
\]
Since the cited limit gives \(T_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)\) and \(R_n=o_P(1)\), taking lower and upper limits and then letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) uses continuity of \(\Phi\) to give \(T_n+R_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)\). Thus the published limits transfer to centering at \(\theta_n\) only on the stated source-class intersection. The nonzero degree-exact remainder proved above also confirms that the two finite-sample targets have not been identified with one another by definition.

statements.statement:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), the oracle bandwidth \(h^\dagger\) is well defined.  For every prespecified \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), the feasible estimator and interval in \({\rm def:estimator}\) and \({\rm def:honest-interval}\) are polynomial-time reportable and, for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), satisfy
\[
 \Pr_Z\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\mid A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\}\geq1-\alpha
\]
for almost every preassignment realization.  Before intersection with \([-B,B]\), their pointwise half-length is exactly \(\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)/\sqrt\alpha\), including every realized degree and isolate.  In particular, \(h=d^{-1}\) is admissible whenever \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\); it is a prespecified operational choice, not an identity with \(h^\dagger\), and receives no optimizer bound by that identity.  At the oracle bandwidth,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{h^\dagger}-\theta_n|
 \leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{h^\dagger}\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{h^\dagger})]
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
The first guarantee is finite-sample conditional certification for a reportable prespecified bandwidth; the displays at \(h^\dagger\) are oracle conservative integrated bounds.  No bandwidth oracle inequality and no comparison \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is asserted.
statements.justification: This theorem separates an operational finite-sample conditional certificate for every prespecified admissible bandwidth from integrated risk and length bounds at the oracle class-supremum optimizer. Unlike Li--Wager's asymptotic PC Gaussian result, it is exact-degree and targets the distinct realized derivative; unlike Armstrong--Kolesar's smooth-regression intervals, it includes random exposure lattices, empirical spectral residualization, and isolates.
statements.gap: The oracle bandwidth is not evaluable without the full-class supremum, and no bandwidth oracle inequality or comparison of the conservative observable envelope with the analytic supported envelope is proved.
statements.consumer: Experimenters may report the certified interval at any prespecified admissible bandwidth, including the endpoint choice \(h=d^{-1}\) when admissible; the \(h^\dagger\) displays are conservative oracle benchmarks rather than an achieved frontier.

statements.statement:
For \(1\leq k\leq r\), let \(I_k=[(k-1)/r,k/r)\), with \(1\) included in \(I_r\), put \(\psi_k(u)=\sqrt r\,\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\), and set
\[
 c_0=\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\},
 \qquad
 W_0(u,v)=c_0\mathbf 1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}.
\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor.  The two displayed compatibility inequalities are only sufficient conditions for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same supported lower benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.justification: The explicit equal-block graphon and three same-class response pairs prove the supported analytic converse under the displayed sufficient compatibility conditions; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.gap: The compatibility inequalities are merely sufficient for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness. This is a limitation of the witness, not a gap in the supported lower benchmark, which \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) establishes over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.consumer: Experimenters may use the supported bandwidth envelope as a certified global lower benchmark whenever the repaired class is eventually nonempty; this theorem additionally provides a concrete equal-block witness when its displayed compatibility conditions hold.
statements.proof_tex:
We first verify the displayed equal-block graphon.  The intervals \(I_1,\ldots,I_r\) partition \([0,1]\) up to null endpoints, so
\[
 \int_0^1\psi_k(u)\psi_\ell(u)\,du
 =r|I_k\cap I_\ell|=\mathbf1\{k=\ell\}.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(T_0\) is the integral operator with kernel \(W_0\), then
\[
 (T_0\psi_k)(u)
 =c_0\mathbf1\{u\in I_k\}\int_{I_k}\sqrt r\,dv
 =\frac{c_0}{r}\psi_k(u).
\tag{2}
\]
The range of \(T_0\) is the span of these \(r\) functions.  Hence \(W_0\) has exact rank \(r\), every nonzero eigenvalue equals \(c_0/r\), and the definition of \(c_0\) gives
\[
 c_0/r\geq\underline\lambda,
 \qquad \int_0^1W_0(u,v)\,dv=c_0/r\geq\kappa^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
The compatibility inequality \(c_0\leq\kappa\) gives \(0\leq W_0\leq\kappa\), and \({\rm ass:edge\text{-}probability}\) then gives \(0\leq\rho_nW_0\leq1\).

Writing Bernstein's moment condition for a centered variable \(X\) as
\[
 \mathbb E|X|^q\leq\frac{q!}{2}\mathbb E(X^2)b_\psi^{q-2},
 \qquad q\geq2,
\tag{4}
\]
we have \(\mathbb E\psi_k(U_i)=r^{-1/2}\).  For \(r\geq2\),
\[
 |\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}|
 \leq(r-1)/\sqrt r\leq b_\psi.
\]
Raising this bound to power \(q-2\), multiplying by the square, and taking expectations proves (4), since \(q!/2\geq1\).  For \(r=1\), the centered eigenfunction is zero.  Equations (1)--(4), together with \({\rm ass:unit\text{-}sampling}\), \({\rm ass:graphon\text{-}draw}\), and \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\), verify every graph, rank, regularity, and design condition in \({\rm def:model\text{-}class}\).

Set \(s_0=B/4>0\), and let independent intercepts \(\xi_i\), independent of the latent types, graph, and assignment, have density
\[
 p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)
 \mathbf1\{|t|\leq s_0\}.
\tag{5}
\]
The substitution \(y=\pi t/(2s_0)\) shows that (5) integrates to one.  For deterministic \(g\in C^3[0,1]\), define
\[
 f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x).
\tag{6}
\]
If
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\leq3B/4,
 \qquad \max_{1\leq j\leq2}\|g^{(j)}\|_\infty\leq B,
 \qquad \|g^{(3)}\|_\infty\leq L,
\tag{7}
\]
then \(|f_i^\pm(a,x)|\leq s_0+3B/4=B\), the derivative conditions in \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) and \({\rm ass:third\text{-}derivative\text{-}bound}\) hold, and the response functions are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws with the required uniform latent-type marginal.  Anonymous interference holds by using (6) in \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\).  Hence both signs lie in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), and \({\rm def:target}\) gives
\[
 \theta_n^\pm=\pm g'(1/2),
 \qquad \Delta_g:=|\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=2|g'(1/2)|.
\tag{8}
\]

Let \(Q_g^\pm\) be the resulting joint laws of \(D=(A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\).  Define \(H^2(p,q)=\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\) and \(\operatorname{TV}(p,q)=\tfrac12\int|p-q|\) for dominated laws.  The square root of (5), extended by zero, is absolutely continuous and satisfies
\[
 \|\{\sqrt{p_{s_0}}\}'\|_2^2=\frac{\pi^2}{4s_0^2}.
\]
The fundamental theorem of calculus and Minkowski's inequality therefore give
\[
 H^2\{p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1),p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\}
 \leq\frac{\pi^2(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Let \(X_i^\circ=1/2+V_i\) for \(N_i>0\) and \(X_i^\circ=0\) for \(N_i=0\).  Conditional on \((A,Z)\), the two outcome densities are independent translations whose locations differ by \(2g(X_i^\circ)\).  Product affinity and \(1-\prod_i(1-x_i)\leq\sum_i x_i\) give, after integration over the common \((A,Z)\)-law,
\[
 H^2(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq\frac{\pi^2}{s_0^2}\mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^ng(X_i^\circ)^2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq H(Q_g^+,Q_g^-).
\tag{10}
\]
The second inequality follows directly by Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(|p-q|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)\).

Put \(\bar c=c_0/r\).  Conditional on the block of \(U_i\), each other independent uniform type falls in that block with probability \(1/r\); integrating the conditionally independent edge draw therefore gives independent incident edges with common probability \(p_n=\bar c d/n\).  Thus
\[
 N_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n),
 \qquad \mu_n=(n-1)p_n\asymp d.
\tag{11}
\]
The binomial identity \(\mathbb E(N_i+1)^{-1}=\{1-(1-p_n)^n\}/(np_n)\), the inequality \(N^{-1}\mathbf1\{N>0\}\leq2(N+1)^{-1}\), and \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\), which gives \(\mathbb E_Z(V_i^2\mid A,N_i=N)=1/(4N)\), imply
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_iV_i^2\mathbf1\{N_i>0\}=O(n/d),
 \qquad n\Pr(N_i=0)=O(ne^{-cd}).
\tag{12}
\]
Take
\[
 g_G(x)=c_GB\sqrt{d/n}\,(x-1/2).
\tag{13}
\]
Because \({\rm ass:sparse\text{-}limit}\) gives \(d/n\to0\), condition (7) holds for all sufficiently large \(n\) when \(0<c_G\leq1\).  Equations (10)--(13) give \(H^2(Q_G^+,Q_G^-)\leq Cc_G^2\).  With \(\eta=(1-2\alpha)/2>0\), choose fixed \(c_G>0\) small enough that
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_G^+,Q_G^-)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \Delta_G=2c_GB\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{14}
\]

For the interior pair, suppose \(L>0\), define
\[
 \phi(t)=t(1-4t^2)^4\mathbf1\{|t|<1/2\},
 \qquad
 g_h(x)=c_ILh^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{h}\right).
\tag{15}
\]
The fourth-order endpoint zeros make the zero extension of \(\phi\) a \(C^3\) function, and \(\phi'(0)=1\).  If \(C_j=\|\phi^{(j)}\|_\infty\), then \(\|g_h^{(j)}\|_\infty=c_ILh^{3-j}C_j\).  Choosing fixed \(c_I>0\) sufficiently small, and using \(h\leq d^{-1/2}\to0\), verifies (7) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

The largest atom of \({\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\) is at most \(CN^{-1/2}\), as follows from the consecutive-central-coefficient induction in the proof of \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\), and \(|M/N-1/2|\leq h\) contains at most \(2Nh+2\) lattice points.  Therefore
\[
 \Pr\{|M/N-1/2|\leq h\mid N\}
 \leq C(\sqrt N\,h+N^{-1/2}).
\tag{16}
\]
For a binomial variable of mean \(\mu\), the exponential-Markov calculation with \(t=\log2\) gives \(\Pr(N<\mu/2)\leq e^{-c\mu}\).  Splitting the inverse moment on this event, using \(\mu_n\asymp d\), and applying Jensen's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb E\sqrt{N_i}\leq C\sqrt d,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\{N_i^{-1/2}\mathbf1(N_i>0)\}\leq Cd^{-1/2}.
\]
Since \(h\geq d^{-1}\), (16) implies
\[
 \Pr(|V_i|\leq h,N_i>0)\leq C\sqrt d\,h.
\tag{17}
\]
The bump vanishes for isolates and outside this event, so (10), (15), and (17) yield
\[
 H^2(Q_h^+,Q_h^-)
 \leq Cc_I^2n\sqrt d\,L^2h^7.
\tag{18}
\]
For \(h_0=\{L^{-2}/(n\sqrt d)\}^{1/7}\) in the interior regime, choose fixed \(c_I\) small enough to obtain
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{h_0}^+,Q_{h_0}^-)\leq\eta,
 \qquad
 \Delta_I=2c_ILh_0^2
 =2c_IL^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{19}
\]

For the lattice pair, fix \(K>e\bar c\), put \(a_K=K\log\{K/(e\bar c)\}>0\), enlarge \(K\) until \(a_KC_{\log}>2\), and set \(D_n=\lceil Kd\rceil\).  Exponential Markov's inequality, \(\mathbb Ee^{tN}\leq\exp\{\mu(e^t-1)\}\), and the choice \(e^t=D_n/\mu\) give \(\Pr(N>D_n)\leq(e\mu/D_n)^{D_n}\).  Applying this with \(\mu=\mu_n\leq\bar c d\) and taking a union bound gives
\[
 \Pr(\max_iN_i>D_n)\leq ne^{-a_Kd}=o(1).
\tag{20}
\]
Set \(w_n=(4D_n)^{-1}\) and
\[
 g_D(x)=c_DLw_n^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{w_n}\right),
\tag{21}
\]
with fixed \(c_D>0\) sufficiently small to make (7) hold.  If \(1\leq N_i\leq D_n\), every noncentral exposure-lattice point has absolute centered value at least \((2D_n)^{-1}>w_n\); at a central point the odd bump is zero, and at an isolate it is also zero.  Thus the two observed laws coincide on \(\{\max_iN_i\leq D_n\}\), and
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_D^+,Q_D^-)
 \leq o(1)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \Delta_D=2c_DLw_n^2\asymp Ld^{-2}.
\tag{22}
\]
This proves membership and the asserted linear, smooth-bump, and lattice witnesses inside the explicit block submodel.  When \(L=0\), the two nonlinear terms are zero and only the linear pair is needed.

For any one of these pairs, an arbitrary real-valued estimator \(T=T(D)\) satisfies
\[
 \max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}\mathbb E_{Q^\sigma}|T-\theta^\sigma|
 \geq\frac\Delta4\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
\tag{23}
\]
Indeed, on the complement of \(\{|T-\theta^+|\geq\Delta/2\}\), the triangle inequality gives \(|T-\theta^-|\geq\Delta/2\); summing the two risks and applying the definition of total variation proves (23).

For the length criterion, let \(\mathcal C(D)=[\ell(D),u(D)]\) be any interval admitted by \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\).  Uniform coverage under the two member laws gives
\[
 Q^+(\theta^+\in\mathcal C)\geq1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 Q^+(\theta^-\in\mathcal C)
 \geq1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-).
\]
The union bound implies
\[
 Q^+\{\theta^+,\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}
 \geq1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-).
\]
On the simultaneous-inclusion event, connectedness and endpoint ordering imply \(u(D)-\ell(D)\geq|\theta^+-\theta^-|=\Delta\).  Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)
 \geq\Delta\{1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
\tag{24}
\]
The interval restriction is used explicitly here.  Equations (14), (19), and (22)--(24) provide the three lower orders for both minimax criteria.

Finally put \(a_n=(n\sqrt d)^{-1/2}\).  The balance relation is
\[
 Lh_0^2=a_nh_0^{-3/2}=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{25}
\]
If \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), evaluation at \(d^{-1}\) and the equivalent inequality \(L^2\geq d^{13/2}/n\) give
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}\leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{26}
\]
If \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), evaluation at \(h_0\) gives at most twice the quantity in (25).  If \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\), then \(L^2\leq d^3/n\), and evaluation at \(d^{-1/2}\) gives at most \(2\sqrt{d/n}\).  For \(L=0\), that endpoint gives exactly \(\sqrt{d/n}\).  Combining the graph pair with the lattice pair in the first regime, with the interior pair in the second, and alone in the third proves
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\tag{27}
\]
The constant may depend on the fixed class constants and \(\alpha\), but is independent of \(n,d\).  The block construction used the two displayed compatibility inequalities only as sufficient membership conditions.  Independently, the same-round proof of \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) proves (27) over every eventually nonempty repaired class.  This establishes the theorem's final sentence without claiming that the block conditions characterize nonemptiness.

statements.statement:
For \(L>0\), at every sufficiently large triangular-array index the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), the oracle conservative envelope proves
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Along every sequence covered by the unrestricted supported converse, there is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the repaired class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph.  No bound \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is proved; hence the three analytic phases are a tuning geometry and a minimax lower benchmark, not an achieved honest expected-length frontier.
statements.justification: This proposition solves the analytic bandwidth optimization and combines the same-class lower benchmark with the oracle conservative upper envelope under their correct nonempty domains.
statements.gap: The bounded-difference certificate has no proved comparison with the analytic supported envelope, so the displayed lower--upper bracket is not known to be tight.
statements.consumer: The three phases support design triage as lower-benchmark and tuning geometry; the upper curve is an oracle conservative benchmark, not a guaranteed reportable confidence-length frontier.

statements.statement:
For the explicit construction in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), all distinct scores over \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) can be represented and computed in polynomial time.  Conditional on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions, for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\),
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \leq\overline b_h(A),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \leq\overline s_h(A)^2.
\]
Consequently \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\}\geq1-\alpha\).  If \(C_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A)A\) and
\[
 G_A(C_A)=\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2,
\]
then the explicit bias certificate also satisfies the deterministic bound
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \leq \frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*
      +B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}{n}}.
\]
The exact first two Hoeffding projections create no bandwidth-dependent term.  This result does not assert the sharper uniform rates \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\); the displayed graph norm and conservative variance certificate are the proved computable quantities under the frozen assumptions.
statements.justification: This gives an explicit polynomial-time first-projection PC estimator and a finite-sample conditional certificate without asserting the unproved sharp spectral remainder rates.
statements.gap: The exact first two Hoeffding projections are benign, but the frozen assumptions do not yet yield the edge-restricted projector norm and sharp product-ANOVA bounds needed for a \(d/n\) variance remainder.
statements.consumer: The observable certificate is safe for experiment reporting; its conservative variance term transparently signals that the sharp confidence-length frontier remains unresolved.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(A\), the preassignment response functions, and \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  All expectations and variances in this proof are over the independent assignment coordinates from \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\).  Put
\[
 X=Z-\frac12\mathbf1_n,\qquad
 P_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A),\qquad
 C_A=P_AA,\qquad
 F_h(Z)=\widehat\theta_h.
\tag{1}
\]
The corrected \({\rm def:empirical\text{-}projector}\) uses \(m_{r,n}=\min\{r,n\}\) eigenvectors.  Hence \(P_A\) is an \(n\times n\) orthogonal spectral projector for every finite \(r,n\); no condition \(r\leq n\) is needed below.

We first prove the variance certificate.  If \(z^{(j)}\) is obtained from \(z\) by flipping coordinate \(j\), the finite maximum in \({\rm def:pc\text{-}handle}\) gives
\[
 |q_{i,h}(z)-q_{i,h}(z^{(j)})|\leq D_{ij,h}.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, the difference is zero when \(A_{ij}=0\); when \(A_{ij}=1\), the treated-neighbor count moves between two consecutive integers occurring in that maximum.  The division by \(\mu_{2,i}(h)\) is valid for \(N_i>0\) by \({\rm lem:exact\text{-}score\text{-}moments}\), and both sides of (2) are zero under the definitions when \(N_i=0\).  Since \(|X_j|=1/2\), the definitions of \(Q_{i,h}\), \(\Gamma_{i,h}\), and \(\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}\) imply
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)|
 \leq Q_{i,h}+2\sum_{j'}|(C_A)_{ij'}|
 =\Gamma_{i,h}.
\tag{3}
\]
A flip changes \(X_j\) by one in absolute value, and therefore
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)-\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z^{(j)})|
 \leq D_{ij,h}+4|(C_A)_{ij}|.
\tag{4}
\]

The response-level part of \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) gives \(|Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)|\leq B\).  If \(j=i\), a flip changes only the own-treatment argument, so the two response values differ by at most \(2B\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), then \(j\ne i\), \(N_i>0\), and the exposure fraction changes by \(N_i^{-1}\).  The first-derivative part of \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) and the fundamental theorem of calculus give
\[
 |f_i(z_i,x+N_i^{-1})-f_i(z_i,x)|
 =\left|\int_x^{x+N_i^{-1}}\partial_t f_i(z_i,t)\,dt\right|
 \leq B/N_i.
\]
In every other case \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\) makes the change zero.  With the zero-degree convention in \({\rm def:pc\text{-}handle}\),
\[
 |Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)-Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z^{(j)})|
 \leq B\left\{2\mathbf1\{i=j\}+\frac{A_{ij}}{N_i}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Applying \(|gy-g'y'|\leq|g-g'||y|+|g'||y-y'|\) to (3)--(5) proves
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)
 -\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z^{(j)})Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z^{(j)})|
 \leq\beta_{ij,h}.
\tag{6}
\]
Summing (6) and using \({\rm def:estimator}\) yields
\[
 |F_h(z)-F_h(z^{(j)})|
 \leq c_{j,h}:=\frac1n\sum_i\beta_{ij,h}.
\tag{7}
\]

Let \(\mathcal F_j=\sigma(Z_1,\ldots,Z_j)\), \(M_j=\mathbb E_Z(F_h\mid\mathcal F_j)\), and \(E_j=M_j-M_{j-1}\).  If \(j<k\), the tower property gives
\[
 \mathbb E_Z(E_jE_k)
 =\mathbb E_Z\{E_j\mathbb E_Z(E_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\}=0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(F_h)=\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E_ZE_j^2.
\tag{8}
\]
Given \(\mathcal F_{j-1}\), the difference between the two values of \(M_j\) obtained by setting \(Z_j=1\) and \(Z_j=0\) is an average over future coordinates of differences bounded by (7), and hence is at most \(c_{j,h}\).  By \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\), these two values have equal conditional probabilities.  The variance of two equal-mass values \(a,b\) is \((a-b)^2/4\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \leq\frac14\sum_jc_{j,h}^2
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_j\left(\sum_i\beta_{ij,h}\right)^2
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 =\overline s_h(A)^2.
\tag{9}
\]

We next prove the bias certificate.  For \(N_i>0\), \(q_{i,h}\) depends only on neighbor assignments and is independent of \(Z_i\), because \(A_{ii}=0\) under \({\rm ass:graphon\text{-}draw}\).  Conditioning first on \(Z_i=a\), applying \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\) and \({\rm lem:exact\text{-}score\text{-}moments}\), and averaging the two equiprobable own-treatment values gives
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 -\frac{\partial_xf_i(1,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(0,1/2)}2\right|
 \leq\frac L6h_i(h)^2.
\tag{10}
\]
For \(N_i=0\), \(q_{i,h}=0\), while the first-derivative part of \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) bounds the absolute target summand by \(B\).  Thus the conditional bias of the score part is at most
\[
 \frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac Bn\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\tag{11}
\]

It remains to bound the PC subtraction.  Centering and \(|Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}|\leq B\) imply
\[
 |\mathbb E_Z[X_iY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]|\leq B/2.
\tag{12}
\]
For \(j\ne i\) with \(A_{ij}=1\), condition on all assignments except \(Z_j\).  The response-change bound in (5) and the two equiprobable values of \(Z_j\) give
\[
 |\mathbb E_Z[X_jY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]|
 =\frac14\left|\mathbb E_Z[Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid Z_j=1]
 -\mathbb E_Z[Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid Z_j=0]\right|
 \leq\frac B{4N_i}.
\tag{13}
\]
If \(j\ne i\) and \(A_{ij}=0\), the expectation is zero by \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\) and \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac4n\sum_i\left|\sum_j(C_A)_{ij}
       \mathbb E_Z[X_jY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]\right|
 &\leq\frac{2B}{n}\sum_i|(C_A)_{ii}|\\
 &\quad+\frac Bn\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
       \sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|\\
 &=\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
Combining (11)--(14) with \({\rm def:target}\), \({\rm def:estimator}\), and \({\rm def:radii}\) proves
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \leq\overline b_h(A).
\tag{15}
\]

Because \(P_A\) is a spectral projector of the symmetric matrix \(A\), it commutes with \(A\); hence \(C_A=P_AA\) is symmetric.  If \(C_A=\sum_t\nu_tu_tu_t^\top\) is its spectral decomposition, orthonormality gives
\[
 \sum_i|(C_A)_{ii}|
 \leq\sum_t|\nu_t|\sum_i u_{t,i}^2
 =\sum_t|\nu_t|=\|C_A\|_*.
\tag{16}
\]
Finite-sum Cauchy--Schwarz within every positive-degree row and then across the at most \(n\) such rows gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|
 &\leq\sum_{i:N_i>0}
 \left\{\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\leq\sqrt{nG_A(C_A)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Substitution of (16)--(17) into \({\rm def:pc\text{-}handle}\) proves
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \leq\frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*+B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}n}.
\tag{18}
\]

Put \(E_h=\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\) and \(m_h=\mathbb E_Z(E_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)\).  If \(\overline s_h(A)>0\), then pointwise
\[
 \mathbf1\{|E_h-m_h|>\overline s_h(A)/\sqrt\alpha\}
 \leq\frac{\alpha(E_h-m_h)^2}{\overline s_h(A)^2}.
\]
Taking conditional expectations and using (9) bounds the probability on the left by \(\alpha\).  If \(\overline s_h(A)=0\), (9) gives \(E_h=m_h\) conditionally almost surely.  Together with (15), in either case
\[
 \Pr_Z\!\left(
 |\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n|>
 \overline b_h(A)+\frac{\overline s_h(A)}{\sqrt\alpha}
 \mathrel{\Big|}A,(f_i)_i\right)\leq\alpha.
\tag{19}
\]
The first-derivative envelope and \({\rm def:target}\) give \(|\theta_n|\leq B\); intersection with \([-B,B]\) therefore cannot remove the target on the event certified in (19).  Integrating the conditional inequality under any \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) proves the asserted uniform coverage.

Finally, for each realized degree the truncated score changes only when \(h\) crosses one of finitely many lattice distances.  Across all units there are at most \(O(n^2)\) such breakpoints.  Exact finite binomial sums compute \(\mu_{2,i}(h)\), the finite maxima compute \(Q_{i,h}\) and \(D_{ij,h}\), one eigendecomposition with the leading \(\min\{r,n\}\) convention computes \(C_A\), and matrix and finite-sum arithmetic compute the remaining certificates.  Thus every distinct score and every certificate at a supplied bandwidth are polynomial-time sample maps.  By \({\rm lem:exact\text{-}score\text{-}hoeffding\text{-}projections}\), the first projection of \(q_h-4P_AAX\) is
\[
 4(I_n-P_A)AX,
\]
and its second projection is zero.  The construction therefore subtracts the empirical leading-eigenspace component; it does not remove the residual first projection.  Neither projection depends on \(h\).  Equations (9), (15), (18), and (19) prove every asserted certificate without imposing a sharper stochastic order.

Along every triangular-array sequence for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty at every sufficiently large index, \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), and \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) are fixed, there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
At each index the proof fixes the graph primitives of an arbitrary admissible member, retains its kernel \(W\) and the independent \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\) latent types, and changes only the response law.  For almost every \(u\),
\[
 N_i\mid U_i=u
 \sim{\rm Binomial}\!\left(n-1,\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv\right),
 \qquad
 \frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{\kappa}
 \leq\mathbb E(N_i\mid U_i=u)
 \leq(n-1)\rho_n\kappa.
\]
These uniform conditional-degree bounds, together with explicit linear, local \(C^3\)-bump, and degree-lattice response pairs, give respectively the graph, interior, and lattice terms for both minimax absolute risk and minimax honest expected length.  No null-row modification or atomic latent-type law is used.
statements.justification: A null-row modification of any admissible integral kernel and an atomic latent-type distribution produce an exact mean-degree \(d\) Erdos--Renyi submodel for every nonempty frozen class; three explicit two-point response experiments then attain all supported-envelope terms.
statements.gap: The positive result uses the literal frozen class, whose latent-type marginal is unrestricted and whose graphon bounds hold almost everywhere; imposing uniform latent types or pointwise graphon constraints would define a different class and would require a new compatibility argument.
statements.consumer: The supported analytic envelope is a global minimax lower benchmark for every nonempty parameter tuple in the frozen model, not only for tuples admitting the equal-block witness.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large index for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), and select the graph primitives \(W\), \((\lambda_k,\psi_k)_{k=1}^r\), and graph sampling law from one admissible member.  We retain those primitives and change only the response law.  Constants below may depend on the fixed class constants and \(\alpha\), but never on \(n\) or \(d\).  Since \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d\) with \(C_{\log}>0\), we have \(d\to\infty\); hence \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) for every sufficiently large index, so all criteria and envelopes used below are defined under their stated nonempty-domain conventions.

Define
\[
 w(u)=\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv,
 \qquad p_n(u)=\rho_nw(u).
\tag{1}
\]
By \({\rm ass:kernel\text{-}bound}\), \({\rm ass:degree\text{-}regularity}\), and \({\rm ass:edge\text{-}probability}\), outside a Lebesgue-null set,
\[
 \kappa^{-1}\leq w(u)\leq\kappa,
 \qquad 0<p_n(u)\leq1.
\tag{2}
\]
The uniform marginal in \({\rm ass:unit\text{-}sampling}\) avoids the exceptional set almost surely.  Conditional on \(U_i=u\), integrating \({\rm ass:graphon\text{-}draw}\) over the independent uniform variables \(U_j\) gives independent edges with common success probability \(p_n(u)\).  Therefore
\[
 N_i\mid U_i=u\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n(u)),
 \qquad m_n(u):=\mathbb E(N_i\mid U_i=u)=(n-1)p_n(u),
\tag{3}
\]
and, because \(\rho_n=d/n\),
\[
 \frac{(n-1)d}{n\kappa}\leq m_n(u)
 \leq\frac{(n-1)d\kappa}{n}.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(d/(2\kappa)\leq m_n(u)\leq\kappa d\) for \(n\geq2\).

We record the degree consequences used below.  If \(N\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p)\), direct expansion of its mass function and the identity \({n-1\choose k}/(k+1)={n\choose k+1}/n\) give
\[
 \mathbb E\frac1{N+1}
 =\frac{1-(1-p)^n}{np}\leq\frac1{np}.
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(N^{-1}\mathbf1\{N>0\}\leq2(N+1)^{-1}\), (2)--(5) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\{N_i^{-1}\mathbf1(N_i>0)\mid U_i=u\}
 \leq\frac{2\kappa}{d}.
\tag{6}
\]
Also,
\[
 \Pr(N_i=0\mid U_i=u)=(1-p_n(u))^{n-1}
 \leq e^{-m_n(u)}\leq e^{-d/(2\kappa)}.
\tag{7}
\]
Conditional on \(A\) and \(N_i=N>0\), \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\) gives \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_Z(V_i^2\mid A,N_i=N)=\frac1{4N}.
\]
Integrating and using (6) yields
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^nV_i^2\mathbf1\{N_i>0\}
 \leq\frac{n\kappa}{2d}.
\tag{8}
\]

For \(M\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\), its largest atom is at most \(C_0N^{-1/2}\).  Indeed, for \(a_q={2q\choose q}4^{-q}\),
\[
 \frac{a_{q+1}}{a_q}=\frac{2q+1}{2q+2},
 \qquad
 \left(\frac{2q+1}{2q+2}\right)^2\leq\frac{q+1}{q+2};
\]
induction gives \(a_q\leq(q+1)^{-1/2}\), and the odd case is bounded by an adjacent even central atom.  The interval \(|M/N-1/2|\leq h\) contains at most \(2Nh+2\) lattice points, whence
\[
 \Pr\{|M/N-1/2|\leq h\mid N\}
 \leq C_1(\sqrt N\,h+N^{-1/2}).
\tag{9}
\]
For a binomial variable \(N\) of mean \(m\), exponential Markov's inequality and the binomial moment-generating function give, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr(N<m/2)
 \leq e^{tm/2}\mathbb E e^{-tN}
 \leq\exp\{tm/2-m(1-e^{-t})\}.
\]
Taking \(t=\log2\) gives
\[
 \Pr(N<m/2)\leq e^{-c_0m},
 \qquad c_0=(1-\log2)/2>0.
\tag{10}
\]
Splitting at \(N_i=m_n(U_i)/2\), and using (4), (10), and \(d\to\infty\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E\{N_i^{-1/2}\mathbf1(N_i>0)\}
 \leq C_2d^{-1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Jensen's inequality and (4) give \(\mathbb E\sqrt{N_i}\leq\sqrt{\kappa d}\).  Combining this with (9), (11), and \(h\geq d^{-1}\) yields, uniformly over \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\),
\[
 \Pr(|V_i|\leq h,N_i>0)\leq C_3\sqrt d\,h.
\tag{12}
\]

Choose \(K>e\kappa\) so large that
\[
 a_K:=K\log\{K/(e\kappa)\}>2/C_{\log},
 \qquad D_n=\lceil Kd\rceil.
\tag{13}
\]
Optimizing exponential Markov's inequality for the binomial law in (3) gives
\[
 \Pr(N_i>D_n\mid U_i=u)
 \leq\left\{\frac{em_n(u)}{D_n}\right\}^{D_n}
 \leq e^{-a_Kd}.
\]
No independence among degrees is needed for the union bound, so \({\rm ass:log\text{-}degree}\) implies
\[
 \Pr\left(\max_iN_i>D_n\right)
 \leq ne^{-a_Kd}
 \leq n^{1-a_KC_{\log}}=o(1).
\tag{14}
\]

We now construct the response experiments.  Set \(s_0=B/4>0\), and let \((\xi_i)\), independently of \((U,A,Z)\), be independent with density
\[
 p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)
 \mathbf1\{|t|\leq s_0\}.
\tag{15}
\]
The substitution \(y=\pi t/(2s_0)\) shows that (15) integrates to one.  For deterministic \(g\in C^3[0,1]\), define
\[
 f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x).
\tag{16}
\]
Whenever
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\leq3B/4,
 \qquad \max_{1\leq j\leq2}\|g^{(j)}\|_\infty\leq B,
 \qquad \|g^{(3)}\|_\infty\leq L,
\tag{17}
\]
the response envelope and third-derivative assumption hold.  The pairs \((U_i,f_i^\pm)\) remain independent and identically distributed with uniform \(U_i\)-marginal, and the retained graph satisfies all other member properties.  Thus each sign in (16) defines a law in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  By \({\rm def:target}\),
\[
 \theta_n^\pm=\pm g'(1/2),
 \qquad \Delta_g:=|\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=2|g'(1/2)|.
\tag{18}
\]
Let \(Q_g^\pm\) denote the resulting joint laws of \(D=(A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\).  For dominated laws with densities \(p,q\), define
\[
 H^2(p,q)=\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2,
 \qquad \operatorname{TV}(p,q)=\frac12\int|p-q|.
\]
Let \(q_{s_0}=\sqrt{p_{s_0}}\), extended by zero.  It is absolutely continuous because the cosine vanishes at both endpoints, and direct integration gives
\[
 \|q_{s_0}'\|_2^2=\frac{\pi^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{19}
\]
For any translations \(\eta_1,\eta_2\), the fundamental theorem of calculus followed by Minkowski's integral inequality gives
\[
 H^2\{p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1),p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\}
 \leq\frac{\pi^2(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{20}
\]
Put \(X_i^\circ=1/2+V_i\) when \(N_i>0\), and \(X_i^\circ=0\) when \(N_i=0\).  Conditional on \((A,Z)\), the two outcome densities for unit \(i\) are translations whose locations differ by \(2g(X_i^\circ)\).  Thus (20) gives \(H_i^2\leq\pi^2g(X_i^\circ)^2/s_0^2\).  If \(a_i=\int\sqrt{p_{i,+}p_{i,-}}=1-H_i^2/2\), conditional independence and Tonelli's theorem give
\[
 H^2\!\left(\bigotimes_i p_{i,+},\bigotimes_i p_{i,-}\right)
 =2\left(1-\prod_i a_i\right)
 \leq\sum_iH_i^2,
\]
where \(1-\prod_i(1-x_i)\leq\sum_i x_i\) for \(x_i\in[0,1]\).  Since \((A,Z)\) is observed and has the same marginal law under both signs, integration over that common law yields
\[
 H^2(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq\frac{\pi^2}{s_0^2}\mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^ng(X_i^\circ)^2.
\tag{21}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(|p-q|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)\leq H(Q_g^+,Q_g^-).
\tag{22}
\]

For the graph-floor pair, take
\[
 g_G(x)=c_GB\sqrt{d/n}\,(x-1/2).
\tag{23}
\]
By \({\rm ass:sparse\text{-}limit}\), condition (17) holds for all sufficiently large \(n\) when \(0<c_G\leq1\) is fixed.  Equations (7), (8), and (23) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\sum_i g_G(X_i^\circ)^2
 &=c_G^2B^2\frac dn
 \left\{\mathbb E\sum_iV_i^2\mathbf1(N_i>0)
 +\frac n4\Pr(N_i=0)\right\}\\
 &\leq C_4c_G^2B^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
\]
Let \(\eta=(1-2\alpha)/2>0\).  Since \(s_0=B/4\), choose a fixed \(c_G>0\) small enough that (21)--(24) give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_G^+,Q_G^-)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \Delta_G=2c_GB\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{25}
\]

For the local nonlinear pair suppose \(L>0\), and define
\[
 \phi(t)=t(1-4t^2)^4\mathbf1\{|t|<1/2\}.
\tag{26}
\]
Its fourth-order endpoint zeros make its zero extension a \(C^3(\mathbb R)\) function, and \(\phi'(0)=1\).  Write \(C_j=\|\phi^{(j)}\|_\infty\), and for \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) set
\[
 g_h(x)=c_ILh^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{h}\right).
\tag{27}
\]
Then \(\|g_h^{(j)}\|_\infty=c_ILh^{3-j}C_j\) for \(0\leq j\leq3\).  Choose \(c_I>0\) so that \(c_IC_3\leq1\), and, if necessary, decrease it so that (17) holds for every sufficiently large \(n\); this is possible because \(h\leq d^{-1/2}\to0\), while \(B,L\) are fixed.  The bump vanishes at the isolate exposure and is supported within \(|V_i|\leq h\).  Hence (12), (21), and (27) give
\[
 H^2(Q_h^+,Q_h^-)
 \leq C_5c_I^2n\sqrt d\,L^2h^7.
\tag{28}
\]
Set
\[
 h_0=\{L^{-2}/(n\sqrt d)\}^{1/7}.
\tag{29}
\]
If \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), substituting (29) into (28) and decreasing \(c_I\) if necessary gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{h_0}^+,Q_{h_0}^-)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \Delta_I=2c_ILh_0^2
 =2c_IL^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{30}
\]

For the lattice pair, continue to suppose \(L>0\), put \(w_n=(4D_n)^{-1}\), and set
\[
 g_D(x)=c_DLw_n^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{w_n}\right),
 \qquad c_DC_3\leq1.
\tag{31}
\]
Because \(D_n\to\infty\), choosing fixed \(c_D>0\) sufficiently small and using the derivative scaling above verifies (17) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(1\leq N_i\leq D_n\), every noncentral exposure point obeys
\[
 |V_i|\geq
 \begin{cases}
 N_i^{-1},&N_i\text{ even},\\
 (2N_i)^{-1},&N_i\text{ odd},
 \end{cases}
 \geq(2D_n)^{-1}>w_n.
\tag{32}
\]
At a central point \(g_D(1/2)=0\) by oddness, and at an isolate \(g_D(0)=0\).  Thus on \(F_n=\{\max_iN_i\leq D_n\}\), the complete observed outcomes under both signs in (16) equal \(\xi_i\).  The restrictions of the two data laws to \(F_n\) agree, and \(F_n\) has the same probability under both.  Therefore (14) gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_D^+,Q_D^-)
 \leq\Pr(F_n^c)=o(1)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \Delta_D=2c_DLw_n^2\asymp Ld^{-2}.
\tag{33}
\]

We reduce these pairs to the two minimax criteria.  For any pair with targets \(\theta^+,\theta^-\), laws \(Q^+,Q^-\), and separation \(\Delta\), define \(A_T=\{|T-\theta^+|\geq\Delta/2\}\).  On \(A_T^c\), the triangle inequality gives \(|T-\theta^-|\geq\Delta/2\), and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}|T-\theta^+|+\mathbb E_{Q^-}|T-\theta^-|
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{Q^+(A_T)+Q^-(A_T^c)\}\\
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{34}
\]
Thus the larger absolute-error risk is at least \(\Delta(1-\eta)/4\).

For honest expected length, \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\) permits data-measurable closed intervals \(\mathcal C(D)=[\ell(D),u(D)]\) with finite ordered endpoints.  Let such an interval satisfy the uniform coverage constraint.  Membership of \(Q^+\) and \(Q^-\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), coverage, and the definition of total variation give
\[
 Q^+(\theta^+\in\mathcal C)\geq1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 Q^+(\theta^-\in\mathcal C)
 \geq1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-).
\]
The union bound therefore yields
\[
 Q^+\{\theta^+,\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}
 \geq1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)
 \geq(1-2\alpha)/2.
\tag{35}
\]
On this simultaneous-inclusion event, connectedness and endpoint ordering force
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{\mathcal C(D)\}=u(D)-\ell(D)
 \geq|\theta^+-\theta^-|=\Delta.
\]
Therefore \(\mathbb E_{Q^+}\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)\geq\Delta(1-2\alpha)/2\).  The interval restriction is used here explicitly; this implication is not asserted for arbitrary disconnected confidence sets.  Equations (25), (30), and (33)--(35), followed by the infima in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\), lower-bound both criteria by fixed multiples of the graph, interior, and lattice separations in their respective regimes.

It remains to compare those separations with the full supported envelope.  Put \(a_n=(n\sqrt d)^{-1/2}\).  For \(L>0\), (29) gives
\[
 Lh_0^2=a_nh_0^{-3/2}=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{36}
\]
If \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), then \(L^2\geq d^{13/2}/n\), so \(a_nd^{3/2}\leq Ld^{-2}\); evaluating at \(h=d^{-1}\) gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}\leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{37}
\]
If \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), evaluation at \(h_0\) gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{38}
\]
If \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\), then \(L^2\leq d^3/n\), so \(Ld^{-1}\leq\sqrt{d/n}\); evaluation at \(h=d^{-1/2}\) gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}\leq2\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{39}
\]
For \(L=0\), the infimum equals \(\sqrt{d/n}\).  Combine the graph and lattice pairs in (37), the graph and interior pairs in (38), and the graph pair alone in (39) and when \(L=0\).  A quantity bounded below by fixed multiples of nonnegative \(x\) and \(y\) is bounded below by a fixed multiple of \(x+y\).  By \({\rm def:frontier\text{-}envelope}\), both minimax criteria consequently satisfy
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
\tag{40}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Every response construction retained the arbitrary admissible kernel and the independent uniform latent types.  All divisions by \(B\), \(d\), or \(N_i\) are justified respectively by \(B>0\), \(d>0\), and restriction to \(N_i>0\); nonlinear constructions are used only when \(L>0\).  This proves the unrestricted converse on every eventually nonempty repaired class under the corrected nonempty-domain definitions.

statements.statement: LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6 is stated conditional on every condition of its Theorem~4: the source's Assumptions~1--5; independent Bernoulli treatment with a fixed probability strictly between zero and one; writing \(G\) for the source graphon, the pointwise row condition that \(g_1(u):=\int_0^1\min\{1,G(u,t)\}\,dt\) is bounded below by a positive constant for every \(u\in[0,1]\); the first- and second-kernel-moment bounds in Theorem~4; and \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1\). Theorem~6 additionally assumes the sparse exponent window \(-1/2<\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)\) and \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)<0\), a rank-\(r\) decomposition, the nonzero ordered-eigenvalue and normalization/orthogonality conditions displayed in equation~(41), and the Bernstein condition displayed in equation~(42). Under all of those source conditions, equation~(43) gives the standardized \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale principal-component-balancing Gaussian limits centered at both the source population indirect effect and the finite indirect effect \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\). This citation record does not assert that every sequence in the maintained class satisfies all of the source conditions.

Conditionally on \(A\), write \(X_j=Z_j-1/2\), \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)^\top\), and \(q_h=(q_{1,h},\ldots,q_{n,h})^\top\).  For a centered scalar function \(g(X)\), define its first projection as \(g^{(1)}=\sum_j\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]\) and its second projection as
\[
 g^{(2)}=\sum_{j<k}\left\{\mathbb E[g\mid X_j,X_k]
 -\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]-\mathbb E[g\mid X_k]\right\},
\]
and apply these definitions coordinatewise to a vector.  The first two conditional Hoeffding projections of the exact-support score satisfy
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX,\qquad q_h^{(2)}=0
\]
simultaneously for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  Consequently, for every \(A\)-measurable orthogonal projector \(\Pi\),
\[
 \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(1)}=4(I_n-\Pi)AX,
 \qquad \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(2)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\!\left[\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2\mid A\right]
 =4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\]

statements.proof_tex:
Condition on \(A\), and put \(X_j=Z_j-1/2\).  The score is centered by \({\rm lem:exact\text{-}score\text{-}moments}\).  Fix \(i\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), the \(N_i\) neighbor contrasts are exchangeable.  Since
\[
 V_i=N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}X_k,
\]
the exact first-moment identity in \({\rm lem:exact\text{-}score\text{-}moments}\) yields
\[
 1=\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_k\mid A]
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_j\mid A].
\]
If \(A_{ij}=0\), then \(q_{i,h}\) is independent of the centered variable \(X_j\), so the same covariance is zero.  A centered function of the symmetric two-point variable \(X_j\in\{-1/2,1/2\}\) is a scalar multiple of \(X_j\).  Because \(\mathbb E_ZX_j^2=1/4\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid X_j,A]
 =4\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_j\mid A]X_j=4A_{ij}X_j.
\]
Summing over \(j\) proves, coordinatewise and simultaneously for all admissible \(h\),
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX.
\]

For the second projection, take distinct \(j,k\).  If either coordinate is not a neighbor of \(i\), independence makes the corresponding two-coordinate interaction zero.  If both are neighbors, let
\[
 H_{jk}(x_j,x_k)=\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid X_j=x_j,X_k=x_k,A].
\]
Simultaneously changing every neighbor contrast to its negative preserves their joint law and changes the odd score to its negative.  Hence
\[
 H_{jk}(-x_j,-x_k)=-H_{jk}(x_j,x_k).
\]
Every function on \(\{-1/2,1/2\}^2\) has a unique Walsh expansion in \(1,x_j,x_k,x_jx_k\).  The displayed oddness forces the coefficients of the even terms \(1\) and \(x_jx_k\) to vanish.  Thus \(H_{jk}\) is the sum of its two one-coordinate conditional expectations, and the \(\{j,k\}\) interaction in the definition of the second projection is zero.  Therefore
\[
 q_h^{(2)}=0.
\]

An \(A\)-measurable linear map preserves Hoeffding order.  Thus, for every \(A\)-measurable orthogonal projector \(\Pi\),
\[
 \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(1)}=4(I_n-\Pi)AX,
 \qquad \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(2)}=0.
\]
Finally, conditional independence under \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\) gives \(\mathbb E_Z[XX^\top\mid A]=I_n/4\).  Symmetry of \(A\) and idempotence and symmetry of \(I_n-\Pi\) then imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_Z\!\left[\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2\mid A\right]
 &=16\operatorname{tr}\!\left((I_n-\Pi)AA^\top(I_n-\Pi)\frac{I_n}{4}\right)\\
 &=4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Let \(I_0(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\).  Under the repaired class, any graph-only radius \(b(A)\) that is required to satisfy
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widetilde\theta-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|\leq b(A)
\]
for every response configuration in the conditional support must obey
\[
 b(A)\geq \frac{B}{n}I_0(A)
\]
on every realized graph.  Whenever \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty, the independent-Rademacher response submodel \(f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx\) is admissible, and even a genie revealing every nonisolate sign leaves, conditionally on \(A\), Bayes absolute-error risk between
\[
 \frac{B}{\sqrt3\,n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \frac{B}{n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}.
\]
Thus the corresponding unconditional missing-sign fluctuation is of order \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\), which is no larger than the expected conditional radius \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\).  This distinction neither constructs an unconditionally honest interval nor proves that every such interval must pay the graph-only conditional radius.
statements.justification: Opposite derivative signs on realized isolates give identical conditional observed laws, while an independent-sign calculation gives the exact square-root-count unconditional fluctuation scale.
statements.gap: The first conclusion is conditional on the graph and response configuration; it does not establish a sharp expected length for all unconditionally honest procedures.

statements.proof_tex:
If \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is empty, the assertions quantified over admissible laws are vacuous.  Suppose it is nonempty.  Retain the latent-type and graph law of one admissible member and replace only its response draw by
\[
 f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx,
 \qquad \varepsilon_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}{\rm Unif}\{-1,1\},
\tag{1}
\]
with the signs independent of latent types, graph variables, and assignments.  The pairs \((U_i,f_i)\) remain independent and identically distributed with uniform \(U_i\)-marginal, as required by \({\rm ass:unit\text{-}sampling}\).  For every displayed argument,
\[
 |f_i(a,x)|\leq B,
 \qquad |\partial_xf_i(a,x)|=B,
 \qquad \partial_x^2f_i(a,x)=\partial_x^3f_i(a,x)=0.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) and \({\rm ass:third\text{-}derivative\text{-}bound}\) hold for every \(L\geq0\); all retained graph and randomization properties are unchanged, and \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\) supplies the potential outcomes.  Hence (1) is an admissible submodel.

Fix a graph \(A\) in the support of this submodel, and set
\[
 S_0(A)=\{i\in\mathcal V_n:N_i=0\},
 \qquad |S_0(A)|=I_0(A).
\tag{3}
\]
Take two sign vectors in the conditional support which agree on \(S_0(A)^c\), with all isolate signs equal to \(+1\) in the first and \(-1\) in the second.  Each vector has positive conditional probability.  If \(i\in S_0(A)\), anonymous interference and (1) give for every assignment
\[
 Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=f_i(Z_i,0)=0.
\tag{4}
\]
The nonisolate responses agree because their signs agree.  Therefore the complete conditional observed-data laws, and hence the conditional mean of any data-measurable estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), are identical under the two configurations.  Denote that common mean by \(m(A)\).  By \({\rm def:target}\),
\[
 \theta_n(\varepsilon)=\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\varepsilon_i,
 \qquad |\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=\frac{2B}{n}I_0(A).
\tag{5}
\]
If a graph-only radius \(b(A)\) bounds the absolute conditional bias for every response configuration in the conditional support, it bounds both \(|m(A)-\theta_n^+|\) and \(|m(A)-\theta_n^-|\).  Thus the triangle inequality gives
\[
 2b(A)\geq|m(A)-\theta_n^+|+|m(A)-\theta_n^-|
 \geq|\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=\frac{2B}{n}I_0(A),
\]
which proves \(b(A)\geq BI_0(A)/n\) on every realized graph in the support.

For the Bayes calculation, reveal \(A\) and all signs on \(S_0(A)^c\).  Conditional on this genie information, the known nonisolate part of the target can be subtracted.  By independence in (1) and the zero observations in (4), all remaining data are independent of
\[
 T_0(A)=\frac Bn\sum_{i\in S_0(A)}\varepsilon_i.
\tag{6}
\]
Writing \(K=I_0(A)\) and \(S_K=\sum_{k=1}^K\varepsilon_k\), the conditional genie Bayes absolute-error risk is
\[
 \frac Bn\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}\mathbb E|S_K-a|.
\]
The law of \(S_K\) is symmetric, and \((|s-a|+|-s-a|)/2\geq|s|\); averaging proves that zero is a Bayes action.  Hence the risk equals \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E|S_K|\).  Independence and centering give
\[
 \mathbb ES_K^2=K,
 \qquad \mathbb ES_K^4=K+6{K\choose2}=3K^2-2K\leq3K^2.
\tag{7}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz yields \(\mathbb E|S_K|\leq\sqrt K\).  H\"older's inequality gives
\[
 K=\mathbb ES_K^2
 \leq(\mathbb E|S_K|)^{2/3}(\mathbb E|S_K|^4)^{1/3},
 \qquad \mathbb E|S_K|\geq\sqrt{K/3}.
\tag{8}
\]
The same inequalities hold at \(K=0\).  Substitution of \(K=I_0(A)\) proves the displayed conditional Bayes-risk bounds.  Averaging over \(A\) gives unconditional scale \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\); since \(\sqrt K\leq K\) for every nonnegative integer \(K\), it is no larger than \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb EI_0(A)\).  This argument neither constructs an unconditionally honest interval nor lower-bounds every such interval, establishing the final scope qualification.

The paper develops design-based asymptotic theory under Bernoulli assignment for Horvitz--Thompson estimators of direct, indirect, and total average treatment effects under uniformly bounded neighbourhood interference, and proposes eigenvector-adjusted point estimators and variance estimators. In contrast, the present note uses a stochastic sparse-graphon model, targets a midpoint derivative on exact realized-degree lattices, proves a finite-sample graph-observable conditional certificate, and gives a same-class smoothness-dependent minimax expected-length lower benchmark without proving a matching feasible upper rate.

tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the new finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, the graph dependence term, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit frontier retains lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. A same-class testing calculation gives only \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) for isolates, whereas the safe interval pays \(B\pi_{0,n}\); therefore no full matched-frontier theorem is claimed. The open content is uniform feasible-PC certification and tail-adaptive completion without minimum-degree or response-sharing assumptions. Li and Wager's Theorem 6 is used only through an explicit finite-to-derivative bridge as an asymptotic benchmark.

project_justification.gap: Li and Wager prove asymptotic normality for a PC estimator of their finite and population indirect effects, but they do not give finite-sample honest length for the distinct realized derivative target or handle exact low-degree support. Standard honest nonparametric theory has no random exposure lattice, graph projector, or latent-type-dependent isolate tail.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a degree-exact, bias-aware statistical frontier for a causal derivative from one network, with observable support diagnostics and an honest distinction between conservative isolate bias and the same-class testing modulus.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact score moments at every positive degree, proves a finite-sample bridge to the published indirect effect, constructs PC-balanced observable radii, establishes supported-unit upper and lower rates plus a degree-tail modulus, and isolates the one remaining tail-adaptation question instead of asserting a false matched frontier.

related_work: LiWager2022RandomGraph is the central asymptotic benchmark. Proposition 1, equations (4)--(5), relates its finite indirect effect to an average derivative through a minimum-degree remainder, and Theorem 6, equation (43), gives a \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale Gaussian limit for its PC estimator in a polynomial-degree sparse regime. The present target \(\theta_n\) is a new realized finite-population derivative; \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) gives the exact degree-level comparison, so no finite-sample same-target tightening is claimed. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect supplies the Bernoulli-policy decomposition and causal interpretation. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest informs the computable smoothness-bias interval geometry, while CaiLow2004Adaptation informs the testing-to-expected-length argument; neither treats network support or spectral residualization. AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise and TangCape2025InfiniteRank inform the empirical-eigenspace analysis but do not control an exact-support causal score. Leung2022NetworkInference concerns locality-based inference for level effects. BhadraSchweinberger2025Survey is cited only as a broad survey of network-interference frameworks; the separate arXiv identifier 2504.06108 is omitted because its current contagion manuscript is not the linear-rate comparator described in the earlier core.
technical_internal_limitation: For \(N_i>0\), the exact score has second moment \(\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\) and third-order bias at most \(Lh_i(h)^2/6\). These identities do not establish the feasible spectral remainders. Isolates have no exposure variation, so the safe interval adds their full derivative envelope. Under i.i.d. preassignment responses, the corresponding same-class testing modulus is smaller, of order \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\); closing that upper--lower gap requires an estimator, not a stronger assumption.
honest_scope: The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target. LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6 is only an asymptotic benchmark after \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\). Every positive realized degree is handled by its exact support radius; isolates remain visible in the certificate. The supported-unit lattice, interior, and graph-floor terms have a proposed matching converse, and the same-class unsupported and low-degree modulus is explicit. A full matched frontier is not claimed because the safe \(B\pi_{0,n}\) upper allowance is not matched by the \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) isolate testing term. The open tail-adaptive construction must retain the i.i.d. \((U_i,f_i)\) class and the stated conditioning convention. Unknown rank, unknown \(L\), simultaneous policy bands, and optimal ego-cluster design remain outside scope.
